name: Congenital Stationary Night Blindness, Riggs Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Riggs Type Congenital Stationary Night Blindness Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Congenital onset of non-progressive night blindness
Electroretinogram (ERG) showing markedly reduced or absent rod responses with normal cone responses
Normal fundus examination without pigmentary changes
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital non-progressive night blindness with characteristic ERG rod dysfunction and normal fundus appearance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: ERG testing is essential to differentiate Riggs type from other forms of CSNB.

pathognomonic.notes: Night blindness present from birth or early infancy
Characteristic ERG pattern diagnostic for Riggs type
searchTerms: very low rod cell responses on eye test

common.symptomName: Normal visual acuity under photopic conditions

common.notes: No pigmentary retinal changes or degeneration
Light sensitivity may be present in some patients

occasional.notes: Involuntary eye movements reported in some cases
Slower adjustment from light to dark environments
searchTerms: difficulty seeing in low light initially

occasional.notes: Occasional perception of flashes of light

rare.notes: Rare cases may show subtle color discrimination abnormalities

rare.symptomName: Photophobia severe enough to impair daily activities

imaging: Normal optical coherence tomography (OCT) of retina
other: Characteristic ERG showing absent or severely reduced rod responses with preserved cone responses

distinguishingFeatures: Schubert-Bornschein type shows electronegative ERG with ON-bipolar cell dysfunction
Often associated with nystagmus and more severe visual impairment
Progressive night blindness with characteristic pigmentary retinal changes
Progressive visual field constriction and eventual loss of visual acuity

redFlags: Progressive visual loss or worsening night blindness
Presence of pigmentary retinal degeneration on fundus exam
Electronegative ERG pattern indicating other retinal dystrophies
references: Dryja TP et al. Mutations in GNAT1 cause Riggs type congenital stationary night blindness. Nat Genet. 2005.
Orphanet: Congenital stationary night blindness, Riggs type. ORPHA:714096
Hamid A et al. Clinical and molecular characterization of congenital stationary night blindness. Prog Retin Eye Res. 2018.
